'''Eric R. Bittner''' {{post-nominals|FRSC}} is a [[theoretical chemist]], physicist, and [[distinguished professor]] of chemical physics at the [[University of Houston]].

== Biography ==
Bittner obtained his B.S. in chemistry and in physics from [[Valparaiso University]] in 1988. From 1988 to 1994 he worked with John C. Light at the [[University of Chicago]] and obtained his Ph.D. thesis in 1994 on ''Quantum Theories of Energy Exchange at the Gas-Surface Interface''. Subsequently, he worked at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] until 1996 as postdoctoral fellow of the [[National Science Foundation]], with Peter J. Rossky as his mentor. He was visiting scholar at [[Stanford University]] from 1995 to 1997, with Hans C. Andersen as his mentor.<ref name="cv">[http://k2.chem.uh.edu/CV-recent.pdf Eric R. Bittner, Curriculum Vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111002195105/http://k2.chem.uh.edu/CV-recent.pdf |date=2011-10-02 }}, University of Houston, downloaded 22. November 2011</ref>

In 1997 he joined the University of Houston as an assistant professor of theoretical chemistry, where he became an associate professor of theoretical chemistry in 2003. In the summer of 2001, he worked as visiting faculty at the Center for Non-Linear Studies at [[Los Alamos National Lab]] and in 2023 he served as the Ulam Distinguished Scholar in the CNLS.<ref name="cv"/> He is currently a professor
in the UH Physics Department.

In 2009 Bittner became the John and Rebecca Moores Distinguished Professor of chemical physics at the [[University of Houston]].<ref>[http://nsm.uh.edu/people/recognition-and-awards/index.php Recognition and awards]
{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426001238/http://nsm.uh.edu/people/recognition-and-awards/index.php |date=2012-04-26 }}, College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Houston, downloaded 23. November 2011</ref><ref>[http://www.uh.edu/giving/opportunities/endowed/chairs-professorships/index.php Endowed Chairs & Professorships] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510150823/http://www.uh.edu/giving/opportunities/endowed/chairs-professorships/index.php |date=2012-05-10 }}, University of Houston, downloaded 23. November 2011</ref><ref>[http://www.uh.edu/provost/shared-interest/awards/recipients-by-award/moores-history/index.php John and Rebecca Moores Professors Award History] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120805184449/http://www.uh.edu/provost/shared-interest/awards/recipients-by-award/moores-history/index.php |date=2012-08-05 }}, Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost, University of Houston, downloaded 23. November 2011</ref>
In 2013, he became the  Hugh Roy and Lillian Cranz Cullen Professor of Physics.

He has worked at the [[University of Cambridge]], the [[École Normale Supérieure]], Paris, and at [[Los Alamos National Lab]]<ref>[https://www.amazon.com/Quantum-Dynamics-Applications-Biological-Materials/dp/1420080539 Author profile] of ''Quantum Dynamics: Application in Biological and Materials Systems'', downloaded 23. November 2011</ref> and has collaborated, among others, with [[Robert E. Wyatt]].<ref name="cv"/>

Eric Bittner is also an Eagle Scout.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

== Work ==
His main research interests lie with the dynamics of molecules in their [[Excited state|excited electronic states]].

Bittner and his co-workers have investigated [[organic semiconductors]], in particular, semi[[conductive polymer]]s, the modulation and tuning of their electronic dynamics due to intramolecular vibrational motions of the polymers, and investigations into [[phonon]] modes.
They have worked on [[energy transfer]] in [[DNA]] molecules using methods of [[molecular dynamics]], [[time-dependent density functional theory]] (TD-DFT) and analytical [[lattice model (physics)|lattice models]].
They have developed a [[quantum hydrodynamics]] approach for computing the energies involved in quantum vibrations in small [[atomic clusters]] by combining the [[de Broglie–Bohm theory|De Broglie–Bohm formulation of quantum mechanics]] and [[Bayesian]] sampling, using this approach also to study quantum aspects of the thermodynamics of small [[rare gas]] clusters in thermal regions close to the clusters' [[melting point]]. 
Furthermore, they used [[supersymmetry]] (SUSY) quantum mechanics for computing excitation energies of quantum systems using [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo calculations]].

His APS Fellowship citation reads: 
''“For developing theoretical and computational descriptions of quantum dynamics in molecular systems, especially for their use in understanding the migration of energy and charge in molecular electronic excited states.”''

Bittner, Department of Chemistry] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805161220/http://k2.chem.uh.edu/ |date=2021-08-05 }}, University of Houston, downloaded 22. *2012 Fulbright Canada Scholar<ref>[http://www.research.uh.edu/Home/Newsletter--Research-Update/Research-Update-Newsletter---Archive/2012/May-June-2012-Newsletter University of Houston, Division of Research: Research Update May/June 2012]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, downloaded 22. June 2012</ref>
*2009 John and Rebecca Moores Professorship.
*2008 University of Houston Research Excellence Award
*2007 to 2008 [[Guggenheim Fellow]]<ref>[http://www.chron.com/neighborhood/heights-news/article/UH-chemist-named-to-Guggenheim-Fellowship-1545350.php UH chemist named to Guggenheim Fellowship] Houston Chronicle, April 25, 2007</ref>

*1999 NSF CAREER Award
*1995 to 1997 NSF Postdoctoral Fellow

The John and Rebecca Moores professorship was awarded to him as recognition for "outstanding work in both research and teaching". In his nomination, special emphasis was placed on his seminal work on [[De Broglie–Bohm theory#Quantum trajectory method|trajectory-base methods for performing quantum mechanical calculations]].<ref>[http://nsm.uh.edu/news-events/stories/2009/0429-facultyawards.php NSM Faculty Awards 2009], downloaded 23. November 2011</ref>
